approach: The paper's exact system is the authors' own fastText C++ supervised trainer, and the repo ships classification-results.sh which downloads the Zhang et al. 8-dataset release and trains/evaluates every Table 1 row, so the plan is plumbing rather than re-implementation: get a working fasttext engine, get AG News in `__label__N` format, then run the authors' configuration `-dim 10 -wordNgrams 2 -epoch 5 -lr <lr> -thread 20`. # Reproduction report — "Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification" (arXiv:1607.01759)

## Target claim C1
Table 1, row *fastText, h = 10, bigram*, column **AG**: test accuracy.

| | value |
|---|---|
| paper target | 92.5 % |
| reproduced (mean of 5 runs) | **92.35 %** (std 0.05, per-seed 92.39 / 92.28 / 92.37 / 92.30 / 92.38) |
| gap | 0.155 % (tolerance 1.0 %) → **PASS** |
| dataset / split | AG News (Zhang et al. 2015 release), official 7,600-line test split |
| engine | fastText 0.9.2 authors' C++ trainer via the official Python binding (`fasttext-wheel==0.9.2`), repo git `1142dc4c4ecbc19cc16eee5cdd28472e689267e6` |
| runtime | 99 s from a completely clean workspace (data prep + lr search + 10 train/test runs) on 20 CPU threads |

Secondary claim **C2** (same config, *no* bigrams): 91.37 % vs paper 91.5 % → PASS.

## How it was run
```
python reproduce.py            # default: prepare data (cached), reuse lr selection, train + test C1 & C2
python reproduce.py --search   # also re-runs the paper's 4-point validation lr grid
python reproduce.py --smoke    # 2k/1k line plumbing test
```
Pipeline: `prepare_data.py` (locate/download AG News, port of the authors' `normalize_text`,
120k train / 7.6k test + 108k/12k train-valid carve) → `fasttext_engine.py` (engine discovery)
→ lr grid {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5} × 3 seeds on the validation holdout → retrain on all 120k with
the argmax lr → `model.test()` on the untouched 7.6k test split → `results/metrics.json`.

Selected lr = **0.25**, validation accuracy 92.42 %; grid means: 0.05 → 91.69, 0.1 → 92.14,
0.25 → 92.42, 0.5 → 92.31. This independently reproduces the value the authors hard-coded for
AG News in `repo/classification-results.sh` (LR[0] = 0.25).

Configuration used (paper Section 3.1 / Table 1): dim = 10 hidden units, wordNgrams = 2 (bigrams),
epoch = 5, bucket = 10M hash bins, minCount = 1, minn = maxn = 0, loss = softmax, thread = 20,
lrUpdateRate = 100 (linear decay).

## Deviations / assumptions (full list in `state/assumption_ledger.json`, A13–A22)
* **bucket = 10,000,000** hashing bins — the authors' own `classification-results.sh` and the
  "only bigrams" branch of Sec. 2.2; the 100M-bin variant (ledger A3) needs ~4 GB per matrix and
  was not affordable on this 15.4 GB host (A15).
* **loss = softmax** instead of the hierarchical-softmax tree of Sec. 2.1; for 4 classes both give
  the exact same argmax (A18).
* The Zhang release has **no validation split**, so a 10 % holdout of the 120k training lines was
  carved with a fixed seed, keeping the 135 byte-identical duplicate articles on one side (A13).
* fastText's asynchronous 20-thread SGD is **not run-to-run deterministic**, so results are the
  mean over 5 seeds with every per-seed value reported (A16).
* Engine is the **prebuilt `fasttext-wheel` 0.9.2** wheel (same upstream C++ source as the cloned
  repo) because the host has no C++ toolchain for `make` / `pip install .` (A14). No re-implementation
  was used; verdict ceiling stays `reproduced`.
* Tokenisation is a faithful port of the authors' `normalize_text()` (A17).
* Not reproduced: C3–C7 (other sentiment datasets) and C8 (YFCC100M tag prediction — the filtered
  split script the paper promises was never released).
